extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and organizations preparing comments on HHS proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting public comments on HHS (and CDC) proposed regulations via the federal rulemaking process. Covers clarity, evidence, procedural steps, and where to submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly communicate and support your position
rubrics_metrics.description: The most helpful comments clearly communicate and support your position, whether you are for or against the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your position explicitly and back it up with reasons or evidence so the agency can understand and weigh your view. Clarity of the central point is emphasized as the overarching helpful attribute of a comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan Ahead (meet the deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period closes at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the date comments are due, and planning ahead helps to ensure that you submit your comments well before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and plan for the official deadline to avoid late submissions. Submitting early reduces risk of missing the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add detail — be constructive and specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive, detailed comments (whether positive or negative) are the most helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific reasoning, examples, data, or explanation rather than brief or purely opinionated statements. Detailed comments are more actionable for agency reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the issues precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly identify which issues you are commenting on within the regulatory action, and provide the page number, column, and/or paragraph from the Federal Register if you are commenting on a particular word, phrase, or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critiquing specific language, cite the exact location in the Federal Register (page/column/paragraph) so reviewers can find and evaluate your point quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence and suggest alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If you disagree with a proposed action, suggest an alternative (including not regulating at all) and include an explanation of how the alternative might meet the same objective or be more effective, as evidence-based information is particularly helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not only criticize; propose viable alternatives and explain with evidence how they would achieve objectives or be superior. Evidence-based reasoning increases the usefulness of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the agency if you have questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions or do not understand a part of the regulatory document, reach out to the agency contact person listed on the document before submitting your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed agency contact to clarify ambiguities or procedural questions prior to filing a comment, which can improve the relevance and accuracy of your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: You don't have to comment on everything
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not have to comment on every issue in a rule. You may select the issues on which you wish to comment or provide a general comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus your effort on the issues that matter most to you or where you can provide substantive input; a targeted comment can be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit comments (use Regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can provide your comments by going to the federal government's regulations website (Regulations.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments through Regulations.gov as the central portal referenced by the Department for receiving public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the Department's specific requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department often requests comments on specific parts of proposed rules. This may be a helpful place to focus your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for and respond to the particular questions or topics the Department highlights in the proposed rule; addressing those requests increases the relevance of your input.

rubrics_metrics.name: CDC-specific contact option
rubrics_metrics.description: You can email CDCRegulations@cdc.gov with questions, comments, or suggestions on how to improve CDC's regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CDC-related regulatory matters, use the provided email address to send questions or suggestions; this is an additional, agency-specific channel for engagement.
